Golden Write-Manifest outputs parse to identical field values in bash; RelativePath separator mapping round-trips (SR-032). bats: tests/bash/manifest_parse.bats.

On a Docker-capable Linux runner, scripts/Invoke-Container.ps1 -Action BuildAndTest builds the image, backs up a read-only source using a separate writable source-state mount, produces a compressed two-file backup with the complete 8-artifact recovery kit, restores it in a second container, and SHA-256 compares both files; CI additionally proves the image survives a `docker save`/-Action Load roundtrip and a publish/pull roundtrip through a throwaway registry, each re-smoke-tested (TC-079).

After a first backup, removing or corrupting FileBackupState.json then re-running with changed source exits 1, leaves backup bytes and MANIFEST.csv untouched, and creates no snapshot (SR-035). Pester: Describe 'Backup history safety gates (SR-035, SR-036)'.

Emptying a previously populated source makes the next run exit 1 with backup and manifest intact; re-running with AllowEmptySource=true performs the delete-all and snapshots the prior state (SR-036). Pester: Describe 'Backup history safety gates (SR-035, SR-036)'.

RECONSTRUCT refuses an origin whose MANIFEST.csv is missing, and refuses compressed rows when 7-Zip is unavailable instead of copying archive bytes under the original name (SR-008/SR-029, HomeHub finding A). Pester: Describe 'Restore dependency preflight (SR-008, SR-029)'.
A manifest RelativePath that escapes the target root is refused, warned, and counted unrestored so the run fails loudly (SR-009/SR-029). Pester: Describe 'Restore target guard (SR-009)'.

Inspection: FileBackup.Common.psm1 seeds SevenZipDefaultPath from FILEBACKUP_7ZIP_PATH with no module-scope Windows path construction (Common.psm1:63); Invoke-Container.ps1 BuildAndTest imports the modules on Linux (SR-037).

Write-Manifest emits MANIFEST.csv.meta beside the manifest with Version=1, Rows equal to the data-row count, Bytes equal to the file length, and XxH128 equal to Get-FileXxHash of the manifest; an empty record set yields Rows=0; rewriting the manifest replaces the sidecar atomically (no .tmp survives) (SR-038). Pester: Describe 'Manifest witness sidecar (SR-038)'.

After two runs, backup.log contains no orphan/not-in-DB WARN for MANIFEST.csv.meta, a nested sub\MANIFEST.csv.meta is backed up and restored as user data (B6), and each Snapshot_<date> folder carries its OWN witness matching its own manifest rather than the backup root's (SR-038/SR-022). Pester: Describe 'Manifest witness is infrastructure (SR-022, SR-038)'.

RECONSTRUCT.ps1 aborts before writing any manifest row when the origin manifest is truncated or byte-edited (witness failure, exit 3) or replaced by non-CSV text (unrecognizable header, exit 2 — precedence 2 > 3), restores normally once the witness is re-stamped, and restores a sidecar-less legacy origin while logging 'unverified'; -RequireWitness turns that absence into the same abort (SR-039). Pester: Describe 'Manifest witness verification on restore (SR-039)'.

reconstruct.sh is the bash twin of TC-068 over a writable fixture copy: a truncated, byte-edited or row-shortened manifest exits 3 with nothing written into the target while a manifest replaced by non-CSV garbage exits 2 via the pre-existing header guard (precedence 2 > 3), the re-stamped copy restores, a sidecar-less origin exits 0 with an 'unverified' warning, and --require-witness makes it exit 3 (SR-039/SR-031). bats: tests/bash/witness.bats.

Invoked as a child process (pwsh -File RECONSTRUCT.ps1 -ExitCode), the PowerShell restorer returns 0 clean, 1 when a row's only data source was deleted, 2 for a target inside the backup and for a missing MANIFEST.csv, 3 for a witness mismatch, and 4 when an archive row's recovery needs an unavailable 7-Zip; the in-process invocation still throws with the existing wording (SR-040). Pester: Describe 'Restore exit-code table (SR-040)'.

reconstruct.sh returns the same five codes for the same five induced conditions as TC-070, and the pre-existing TC-055 expectations (0 clean, 1 incomplete, 1 traversal, 2 corrupt/unrecognized manifest header) are unchanged (SR-040/SR-031). bats: tests/bash/exit_codes.bats + tests/bash/fail_loudly.bats.

Find-DataFileByHash returns a distinct Cause for each of the four collapsed failures and RECONSTRUCT.log carries a distinct message per cause, with the terminating summary naming the count per class instead of one 'cannot recover by hash' line (SR-040, HomeHub finding D). Pester: Describe 'Hash-recovery failure causes are distinguishable (SR-040)'.

With two data files held unmovable during one run, backup.log records an ERROR per failure plus a summary count, every other entry is still staged, the dated snapshot is still finalized, the run exits 1, no Temp staging folder survives, and the following run completes normally instead of tripping the SR-017 stale-staging guard (SR-041). Pester: Describe 'Move loops aggregate failures (SR-041)'.

Import-BackupConfiguration accepts container/FileBackup.example.json verbatim -- the checked-in file itself, with no in-memory patching and no filesystem access -- returning ConfigVersion 1 and one set; every accepted fixture in the ONE shared corpus (tests/Common/ConfigFixtures.ps1, also driven by TC-075 and TC-077) loads, including a single bare BackupSets object (wrapped, matching the schema's anyOf) and an integral-valued ConfigVersion number (JSON has one number type, so 1.0 IS 1); a minimal JSON config omitting SourceStatePath and AllowEmptySource yields SourceStatePath equal to SourcePath and AllowEmptySource false; a lowercase HashRecalcFreq is normalized to upper; the CLIXML configs written by tests/Common/Harness.ps1 still load with identical field values (SR-042). Pester: Describe 'Configuration loader accepts the documented contract (SR-042)'.

Every defective JSON config in the shared corpus (tests/Common/ConfigFixtures.ps1) is refused by a terminating error naming the offending key by its JSON path (with the set's REAL index, not a literal [?]) and the expected type or value set. EVERY schema-defined value is type-checked, not just the two booleans: a quoted "false" is rejected for CompressEnabled, PreserveFolderTree AND AllowEmptySource (where [bool]'false' is $true, which would silently disarm the SR-036 delete-all refusal), an array or number where a string belongs is rejected (SourcePath, Name, SourceStatePath, HashRecalcFreq, Tools.SevenZipPath, Secrets strings), Secrets.SmtpPort must be an integer, and an out-of-range ConfigVersion is refused as an unsupported version rather than by fractional-representation luck; "AllowEmptySources" is rejected as an unknown key rather than silently ignored; the existing wordings 'at least one BackupSets entry', 'must define a non-empty', and 'invalid HashRecalcFreq' are preserved. No backup, change, state or log artifact is created by any refused run -- in particular a refused run never creates a log directory and never truncates the previous run's global log (SR-042). Pester: Describe 'Configuration loader fails loudly and names the key (SR-042)'.

The shipped container/FileBackup.example.json is loaded, has ONLY its SourcePath/SourceStatePath/BackupPath/ChangePath and Tools.SevenZipPath retargeted to the test drive and host 7-Zip (every other key kept verbatim), and drives a real FileBackup.ps1 run that produces MANIFEST.csv plus the restore kit and restores byte-exact; a keys-only diff proves the executed document is key-identical to the checked-in example, so the example can no longer drift from the contract (SR-042/SR-034). The keys-only diff is host-independent and runs BEFORE the 7-Zip skip guard, so a runner without 7-Zip still catches example drift; CI's unit job asserts 7-Zip is present so the run half cannot silently skip. Pester: Describe 'The shipped example config is executable (SR-042)'.

container/FileBackup.schema.json accepts (via Test-Json, given the JSON and the schema as STRINGS -- the -Path/-SchemaFile forms need pwsh 7.4, above this repo's PowerShell 7+ floor) every fixture the validator accepts and rejects every fixture it rejects, reading the ONE shared corpus tests/Common/ConfigFixtures.ps1 that TC-074/TC-075 drive, so the published schema and the runtime validator cannot drift and the fixture lists cannot be hand-copied out of sync; the schema's BackupSets anyOf and ConfigVersion const agree with the validator on a bare single set object and on an integral-valued version number; container/FileBackup.example.json, the README JSON block, and Invoke-Container.ps1's New-SmokeConfiguration all declare ConfigVersion equal to the loader's supported maximum (SR-042). Pester: Describe 'Published JSON schema matches the validator (SR-042)'.

Run as a child process with -ExitCode, a schema-violating config returns 2 with no backup artifacts created, a MISSING or unsupported-extension config file also returns 2 (the likeliest container misconfiguration -- NagLight must not retry forever on exit 1), a config whose only set fails returns 1, and a clean single-set run returns 0; a refused run leaves a seeded global log byte-intact and creates no log directory at a fresh path; the same invocations without -ExitCode return the pre-change codes and the in-process '& $entry' call still throws for a bad config; a two-set JSON config logs the IF-001 one-set-per-invocation warning naming the count while still processing both sets (SR-043). Pester: Describe 'Entry-point status codes (SR-043)'.

On the ubuntu-latest container CI job, scripts/Invoke-Container.ps1 -Action Export followed by docker rmi and -Action Load reproduces a working image verified by -Action Test; separately, -Action Publish to a throwaway registry:2 service followed by docker rmi (both tags) and -Action Pull reproduces a working image verified by -Action Test. Both roundtrips run in the same job, teardown via the registry service's automatic container lifecycle.

The container smoke test's kit check lists all 8 real kit artifacts (adds RECONSTRUCT.paths.json to the existing 7). After the first no-snapshot backup and its restore, the source is mutated (one file changed, one removed, one added) and the container is run a second time; exactly one Snapshot_<date> folder appears under /changes with its own complete kit; a restore container reconstructs the latest state from /backup and byte-compares it against the mutated source; a second restore container invokes RECONSTRUCT.ps1 from inside the snapshot folder itself and byte-compares its output against the pre-mutation source (SR-010 point-in-time authority).

In each of the four storage modes, a timeline is built in which the newest snapshot holds the only physical copy of content an older snapshot's blank-DataPath row needs; pruning it re-homes exactly that file into the elected destination with the SOURCE row's Compressed/StoredAsHashSize adopted on the destination row, the re-homed content hashes to the row's xxH2Hash at its Length, and every remaining dated state plus the latest state restores byte-exact (exit 0). Pester: Describe 'Prune re-homes the last copy before deleting (SR-045)'.

TC-049's delete / reintroduce-identical / delete-again timeline extended with prunes: pruning the keeper snapshot leaves the content stored exactly ONCE on the quiescent state and every remaining state restorable; pruning oldest-first copies zero bytes; a nested MANIFEST.csv in the fixture stays user data (B6). Runs in the G9-Rollback integration suite across the four modes.

The transaction is interrupted at each phase boundary (the materialized .fbprune.tmp left behind, the destination manifest published but the folder not yet renamed, the folder renamed to Pruning_* but not yet deleted): every dated state still restores byte-exact from every origin, the residue is invisible to both restorers' ^Snapshot_ pattern, and simply re-invoking the command completes the operation and sweeps the residue -- with no journal file anywhere in the store. Pester: Describe 'Prune is idempotent and resumable (SR-046)'.

Each of the ten induced refusals returns its documented SR-040 code (3 for the witness pair, 2 for the rest, 4 for an induced copy I/O failure) and leaves the store byte-identical -- a recursive file-hash comparison covering FileBackupState.json, every manifest and every witness. -AllowUnverifiedIndex and -DiscardUnreferencedData convert their own refusals into warned successes. Manifests tampered with on purpose are re-stamped with Write-ManifestWitness so the failure observed is the one intended and not exit 3 (AGENTS.md 3). Pester: Describe 'Prune refuses before mutating (SR-046)'.

After prunes that re-home into the backup root and into a surviving snapshot, Test-ManifestWitness reports Verified for EVERY manifest in the pool and Reconstruct.ps1 -RequireWitness exits 0 from each origin; no MANIFEST.csv.meta is ever copied between folders. Source guard over the prune path: no Export-Csv and no direct Write-ManifestWitness call. Pester: Describe 'Prune re-stamps every manifest it rewrites (SR-038)'.

Column-wise before/after comparison of every manifest in the pool across the four storage modes: the row sets are identical (same count, same RelativePath order), the six logical columns RelativePath/Length/LastWriteTimeStr/xxH2Hash/Duplicate/MediaMBPerSec are unchanged in every row of every folder, and the only differences are DataPath/Compressed/StoredAsHashSize in the rows the plan named. Pester: Describe 'Prune changes only the storage-form columns (SR-045)'.

Get-BackupSnapshot returns one record per snapshot with all six fields, PhysicalBytes = BytesReclaimed + BytesReHomed, Rows equal to the snapshot's own manifest row count, and a Date parsed from the folder name; the reported BytesReclaimed equals the measured whole-store byte drop after actually removing that snapshot, once the few bytes a destination manifest and its witness gain from the written DataPath are accounted for explicitly (index, not content) and BytesReHomed equals the measured bytes copied; running the report leaves every file in the store byte-identical; the records serialize to one JSON object per snapshot carrying all six fields; the oldest snapshot's plan re-homes nothing while the newest's does. Pester: Describe 'Snapshot inventory reports true dedup-aware reclaim (SR-047)'.

In-container (Docker CI job): the snapshots action emits parseable JSON and exits 0 modifying nothing; pruning a valid snapshot name exits 0 and every remaining state restores byte-exact in-container; an unknown name exits 2 with the tree unchanged; a dry run exits 0 changing nothing; the default action and a flags-only invocation are byte-identical in behavior to today (TC-060/TC-076 re-run unchanged). Locally runnable halves, which DO run in the Pester suite: the entrypoint's action dispatch and '-'-prefixed pass-through parsed out of container/entrypoint.sh, the -Action/-Snapshot parameter contract on FileBackup.ps1, and the grep guard proving bash/reconstruct.sh carries no removal path. The in-container half awaits the Docker CI job.

Regression pin for the Get-BackupContentIndex extraction, run green against the PRE-refactor code: over a hand-built pool Optimize-ChangeFolders keeps the backup copy as keeper, elects the newest snapshot when there is no root copy, deletes no backup-root file, blanks every row whose data file is gone, leaves the row sets otherwise untouched, re-witnesses every manifest it rewrites, and leaves exactly one physical copy per (hash,length) (TC-049's property); an empty change root is a no-op that does not even rewrite the backup manifest. Pester: Describe 'Optimize-ChangeFolders is unchanged by the shared index (SR-026)'.

Over a four-snapshot timeline, pruning at every timeline position: the oldest copies zero bytes, the newest re-homes its superseded bytes, and the middle and the sole remaining snapshot both succeed -- no refusal for the newest or the last. Every case leaves each remaining dated state and the latest state restorable byte-exact and exactly one physical copy per live (hash,length). Runs in the G9-Rollback integration suite.

REPRO-FIRST (red before any WP5 code): with 7-Zip present, each malformed row survives a full backup run untouched by Sync-BackupStorageLayout - the metadata-only comparison at Engine.psm1:529 leaves flag-over-raw and flag-over-archive rows byte-identical and reports the set as successful, and a Compressed=Yes-over-raw row whose configuration now says No produces only a logged ERROR while the set still succeeds. Manifests are re-stamped with Write-ManifestWitness after tampering so the intended failure is observed, not exit 3. Pester: Describe 'Sync-BackupStorageLayout trusts metadata over bytes (SR-049)'.

REPRO-FIRST for the WP4-surfaced latent defect, with NO tampering: run with compression off, supersede a file to create a snapshot, then re-run with compression on so only the backup root migrates. Before the fix, restoring that snapshot writes 7z container bytes under the original filename and exits 0; after the fix the restored bytes equal the original exactly and the exit is 0. The reverse flip, which before the fix exits 4 with a misfiled host-class cause, likewise restores byte-exact. Both restorers. In G9-Rollback plus a bats counterpart.

The verification action reports one finding per disagreeing row across the backup root and every snapshot, mutates nothing (pre/post hash of every file in the tree, including MANIFEST.csv and its witness), and maps its outcome onto the SR-040 table: 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 precondition (missing manifest, -Deep without 7-Zip), 3 witness failure, 4 host. A clean backup in each of the four modes reports zero findings. Describe 'Storage-form verification reports without mutating (SR-049)'.

Repair mode makes every unambiguous finding agree, leaves the six logical columns byte-identical, re-stamps every rewritten folder's witness (Test-ManifestWitness = Verified for every pool manifest; Reconstruct.ps1 -RequireWitness exits 0 from each origin), never re-packs content (data-file payload hashes unchanged), and reports blank-row form disagreements without repairing them. A backup run immediately after a repair is idempotent (SR-024): its manifest rows are byte-identical to a run with no repair in between. Source guard: no verification or repair symbol is reachable from Invoke-BackupSet, and the repair path contains no Export-Csv and no direct Write-ManifestWitness call.

Two rows with identical content and different extensions share one DataPath; a configuration change that flips only one of them to 'wrong' must not delete the file the other still references: after the migration every manifest row resolves, the latest state restores byte-exact with exit 0, and the content is still stored exactly once per (hash,length) on the quiescent state. A forced transformation failure fails the backup set instead of being logged only. Describe 'Layout migration is refcount-safe (SR-051)'.

Test-ShouldCompress returns false for every extension in the merged already-compressed list - the original seventeen plus .jar .tgz .zst .gif .webm .ogg .sav .pack - is case-insensitive, inspects the extension and not the path, and still returns true for compressible extensions including .docx and .txt (SN-003's acceptance line). Parity guard: the list is defined in exactly one place and its documented form in README/AGENTS matches it. Amends TC-002 rather than replacing it.

The extension-list merge at scale: a compression-enabled backup seeded with .gif .webm .jar .tgz .zst .ogg .sav .pack content plus text, run to produce two snapshots on the pre-merge list, is re-run on the merged list. The triggered migration decompresses every affected root row, leaves no dangling reference, and afterwards EVERY state - both snapshots and the latest - restores byte-exact with exit 0 in both restorers; a third run is idempotent (SR-024) and the storage-form verification reports zero findings. Suite case G4.2.

Reconstruct.ps1: a blank-DataPath row whose only pool match is the opposite form restores the true original bytes and exits 0 in both directions; an archive candidate that cannot be expanded but whose raw bytes match (hash,length) is recovered rather than reported as a candidate error; a row with a non-blank DataPath is still resolved by its own Compressed column; genuinely missing content still exits 1 and a genuine host failure still exits 4. Describe 'Hash recovery trusts the located file's form (SR-050)'.

bash/reconstruct.sh mirrors TC-098 exactly under bats: find_by_hash reports the located form, the restore loop consults it, byte-exact output in both directions, unchanged exit codes for content-missing and host classes, shellcheck clean. In tests/bash.

A backup set whose estimated additions exceed the destination volume's free space (induced by a stubbed free-space probe) refuses before any mutation: the backup root, change root and FileBackupState.json are byte-identical to before the run, the message names volume, required and free bytes, and the entry point reports a failed set. A set that fits proceeds unchanged, and a pending storage-layout migration is included in the estimate. Describe 'Backup capacity preflight refuses before mutating (SR-052)'.
